speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the rash on your scalp and forehead in detail: is it itchy, painful, or scaly, and how long has it been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the rash on your scalp thicker or more prominent than the redness on your forehead? Also, have you noticed any silvery scales or family history of eczema? REQUEST TEST: Skin_biopsy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis (presenting atypically as "cradle cap" with erythematous patches and greasy yellow scales, potentially confused with tuberculosis by a misdiagnosing provider).

Please clarify: Is the rash greasy or dry to the touch, and does it respond to mild steroid creams or antifungals? REQUEST IMAGES: Scalp_and_forehead_close_up.
